subject: general
question: In a right triangle ABC, right angled at B, altitude BD is drawn to the hypotenuse AC of the triangle. If AD = 6 cm, CD = 5 cm, then find the value of AB² + BD² (in cm).
solution:
Given:

ABC is a right-angled triangle BD is perpendicular to AC.

AD = 6 cm and DC = 5 cm

Concept used:

ΔABC is a right-angled triangle at B.

BD is perpendicular to AC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb60c384223d2c963bbede27dc74044078e348bcc4554a43b8795202caed850d.png] 

So, ΔABD ~ ΔACB ~ Δ BCD

Now, BD2 = AD × DC and AB2 = AD × AC

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66f2897c02992e7d10b882dd983064bb8c0b4b67ea1d671d6ad105ccaa20f027.png] 

According to the concept,

BD2 = AD × DC

⇒ BD2 = 6 × 5

⇒ BD2 = 30

According to the concept,

AB² = AD × AC

⇒ AB2 = 6 × (AD + CD)

⇒ AB2 = 6 × (6 + 5)

⇒ AB2 = 6 × 11

⇒ AB2 = 66

Now, AB2 + BD2 = 30 + 66 = 96

**∴ The value of AB2 + BD2 is 96 cm. **
